findings.title: 1. BLOCKING — a pid-null starting record can be cleared while its broker lives
findings.body: If the PID save fails and failed-start teardown cannot confirm the child's exit, abandonStart keeps a starting record with pid:null. On the next request, this stale path omits state when calling teardownBrokerSession, treats no-pid as settled, and clears the record. The still-live broker can then be included in a worker tree kill without a broker exclusion.
findings.recommendation: Keep a pid-null starting claim until exit is proved, or recover and save the broker's PID and identity before permitting replacement.

findings.title: 2. BLOCKING — stale teardown can kill a broker that just became ready
findings.body: The re-read compares endpoint, PID, and identity but not state; it then releases the lock before killing. If the starter promotes the same claim to ready after this check, the stale caller can kill a broker that has begun serving a client, and the endpoint-only clear removes its ready record. The stale timing existed on POSIX before v1.4.1; the new Windows kill path makes it destructive there too.
findings.recommendation: Reserve teardown under the state lock so ready promotion cannot succeed afterward, then clear only that exact claim.

findings.title: 3. SHOULD-FIX — a reachable broker can remain starting indefinitely
findings.body: A crashed starter or failed ready-record save can leave a listening broker marked starting, possibly without a saved identity. This path returns that record solely because its endpoint responds; no later caller promotes or verifies it. Windows cancel then refuses worker kills when the identity is absent, while SessionEnd always retains the starting record if graceful shutdown stalls.
findings.recommendation: Verify and promote an adopted starting broker under the lock; otherwise keep the claim and use direct transport.

next_steps: Fix the two ownership blockers and add failure and transition race checks.
Rerun native Windows end-to-end coverage and adversarial review before release.

storedJob.rendered:
# Codex Adversarial Review

Target: branch diff against main
Verdict: needs-attention

DO-NOT-SHIP: a67942d still allows a live broker to lose its ownership record or be killed during the starting-to-ready transition. This was a read-only source review.

Findings:
- [high] 1. BLOCKING — a pid-null starting record can be cleared while its broker lives (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs:305-327)
  If the PID save fails and failed-start teardown cannot confirm the child's exit, abandonStart keeps a starting record with pid:null. On the next request, this stale path omits state when calling teardownBrokerSession, treats no-pid as settled, and clears the record. The still-live broker can then be included in a worker tree kill without a broker exclusion.
  Recommendation: Keep a pid-null starting claim until exit is proved, or recover and save the broker's PID and identity before permitting replacement.
- [high] 2. BLOCKING — stale teardown can kill a broker that just became ready (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs:294-327)
  The re-read compares endpoint, PID, and identity but not state; it then releases the lock before killing. If the starter promotes the same claim to ready after this check, the stale caller can kill a broker that has begun serving a client, and the endpoint-only clear removes its ready record. The stale timing existed on POSIX before v1.4.1; the new Windows kill path makes it destructive there too.
  Recommendation: Reserve teardown under the state lock so ready promotion cannot succeed afterward, then clear only that exact claim.
- [medium] 3. SHOULD-FIX — a reachable broker can remain starting indefinitely (plugins/codex/scripts/lib/broker-lifecycle.mjs:276-291)
  A crashed starter or failed ready-record save can leave a listening broker marked starting, possibly without a saved identity. This path returns that record solely because its endpoint responds; no later caller promotes or verifies it. Windows cancel then refuses worker kills when the identity is absent, while SessionEnd always retains the starting record if graceful shutdown stalls.
  Recommendation: Verify and promote an adopted starting broker under the lock; otherwise keep the claim and use direct transport.

Next steps:
- Fix the two ownership blockers and add failure and transition race checks.
- Rerun native Windows end-to-end coverage and adversarial review before release.
